title: The Oath of Citizenship
summary: The words of the Oath of Citizenship in English and French, and why Canadians pledge their loyalty to the Sovereign rather than to a document, a flag or a country.

sections.title: The Oath of Citizenship

blocks.text:
I swear (or affirm)
That I will be faithful
And bear true allegiance
To Her Majesty
Queen Elizabeth the Second
Queen of Canada
Her Heirs and Successors
And that I will faithfully observe
The laws of Canada
Including the Constitution
Which recognizes and affirms
The Aboriginal and treaty rights of
First Nations, Inuit and Métis peoples
And fulfil my duties
As a Canadian citizen.

Je jure (ou j’affirme solennellement)
Que je serai fidèle
Et porterai sincère allégeance
À Sa Majesté
La reine Elizabeth Deux
Reine du Canada
À ses héritiers et successeurs
Que j’observerai fidèlement
Les lois du Canada
Y compris la Constitution
Qui reconnaît et confirme les droits
Ancestraux ou issus de traités
Des Premières Nations, des Inuits et des Métis
Et que je remplirai loyalement
Mes obligations
De citoyen canadien.

Since 8 September 2022 the Sovereign is King Charles III. The official online Oath now reads "To His Majesty King Charles the Third, King of Canada, His Heirs and Successors". The words above are the 2021 print.

focus: The Oath may be sworn or affirmed: it begins "I swear (or affirm)".
In the Oath you promise to be faithful and bear true allegiance to the Sovereign (King or Queen) of Canada, their Heirs and Successors.
In the Oath you promise to faithfully observe the laws of Canada, including the Constitution.
The Constitution recognizes and affirms the Aboriginal and treaty rights of First Nations, Inuit and Métis peoples.
The Oath ends with a promise to fulfil my duties as a Canadian citizen.
In French the Oath is called Le serment de citoyenneté.

sections.title: Understanding the Oath

blocks.text: In Canada, we profess our loyalty to a person who represents all Canadians and not to a document such as a constitution, a banner such as a flag, or a geopolitical entity such as a country. In our constitutional monarchy, these elements are encompassed by the Sovereign (Queen or King). It is a remarkably simple yet powerful principle: Canada is personified by the Sovereign just as the Sovereign is personified by Canada.

focus: In Canada, we profess our loyalty to a person who represents all Canadians, not to a document, a flag or a country.

quiz.q: In the Oath of Citizenship, to whom do you swear or affirm to be faithful and bear true allegiance?
choices: The laws of Canada, which you promise to faithfully observe as a Canadian citizen
The Constitution of Canada, which recognizes and affirms Aboriginal and treaty rights
The Sovereign (King or Queen) of Canada, and the Sovereign's Heirs and Successors
A geopolitical entity such as a country, or a banner such as the Canadian flag
quiz.why: The Oath pledges to "bear true allegiance to Her Majesty ... Queen of Canada, Her Heirs and Successors", that is, to the Sovereign.

quiz.q: In the Oath of Citizenship, what do you promise to faithfully observe?
choices: The laws of Canada, including the Constitution
The customs of your country of origin
The decisions of the Prime Minister
The laws of your province only
quiz.why: The Oath says "I will faithfully observe the laws of Canada including the Constitution".

quiz.q: According to the Oath, the Constitution recognizes and affirms the Aboriginal and treaty rights of which peoples?
choices: Immigrants and refugees
English and French Canadians
First Nations, Inuit and Métis peoples
Members of the Canadian Forces
quiz.why: The Oath names "the Aboriginal and treaty rights of First Nations, Inuit and Métis peoples".

quiz.q: How does the Oath of Citizenship end?
choices: ...and defend the borders of Canada.
...and vote in every election.
...and respect the Canadian flag.
...and fulfil my duties as a Canadian citizen.
quiz.why: The last line of the Oath is "And fulfil my duties as a Canadian citizen."

quiz.q: In Canada, to whom or what do we profess our loyalty?
choices: A document such as a constitution
A person who represents all Canadians
A banner such as a flag
A geopolitical entity such as a country
quiz.why: The booklet says we profess our loyalty "to a person who represents all Canadians and not to a document ... a banner ... or a geopolitical entity".

quiz.q: In Canada's constitutional monarchy, the constitution, the flag and the country are all encompassed by:
choices: Parliament
The Supreme Court
The Sovereign (Queen or King)
The Governor General
quiz.why: The booklet says "these elements are encompassed by the Sovereign (Queen or King)".

quiz.q: Which statement expresses the principle described in "Understanding the Oath"?
choices: Canadians profess their loyalty to a document such as a constitution, not to a person.
Canada is personified by the Sovereign just as the Sovereign is personified by Canada.
Canadians profess their loyalty to a banner such as a flag that represents all Canadians.
Canadians profess their loyalty to a geopolitical entity such as a country, not to a person.
quiz.why: The booklet calls it "a remarkably simple yet powerful principle: Canada is personified by the Sovereign just as the Sovereign is personified by Canada."

quiz.q: The Oath of Citizenship begins with the words:
choices: I promise
I swear (or affirm)
I pledge allegiance
I declare
quiz.why: The Oath opens with "I swear (or affirm) That I will be faithful".
